title: Bar chart race
description: Ranked horizontal bars that grow, then re-order smoothly over time as the data steps through keyframes: bars overtake each other, values roll, the leader changes, and a big faded period label (year, quarter) changes behind them.
useFor: Rankings over time: market share by year, top products by quarter, followers by month, league tables, "who is winning" stories. Give the names once and one values row per period in `frames`.

names.doc: one name per bar; colours follow the name index so a bar keeps its colour while it moves

frames.doc: keyframes [{label, values[]}] — one values row per period, same order as names

topN.doc: how many bars are visible at a time (others slide off the bottom)

subtitle.doc: small line under the headline (empty = none)

stepFrames.doc: frames per keyframe step at speed 1

scale.doc: "dynamic" rescales to the current leader, "fixed" keeps one scale for the whole race

showRank.doc: print the live rank number at the left

showPeriod.doc: big faded period label behind the bars

startAt.doc: frame the bars start to grow

title: Bubble scatter grow
description: A bubble chart: axes and grid fade in, then bubbles grow in from left to right at their x / y position with area proportional to size, coloured per group, with collision-aware labels and an optional highlighted bubble with a ring.
useFor: Three-variable comparisons: markets by size, growth and margin, countries, products, campaigns, startups. Pass points as [{label, x, y, size, group?, color?}], axis titles and number formats; works on a transparent background.

points.doc: bubbles [{label, x, y, size, group?, color?}]; group sets the colour and builds the legend

subtitle.doc: small line under the headline (empty = none)

sizeLabel.doc: small note about what the bubble size means (empty = none)

zeroBased.doc: start both axes at zero (false zooms to the data range)

showLabels.doc: print bubble labels (inside when they fit, else beside, skipping collisions)

labelTop.doc: only label the N largest bubbles (0 = all that fit)

maxRadius.doc: radius of the largest bubble in u (capped to the plot size)

highlight.doc: label of a bubble to ring and spotlight at the end (empty = none)

colors.doc: palette for groups / bubbles without their own colour

background.doc: page colour, or "transparent" to sit over other content

startAt.doc: frame the axes start to appear

title: Comparison dumbbell
description: A dumbbell (before / after) chart: for each category a "before" dot appears on a shared axis, then the "after" dot slides away from it, stretching a connector coloured green for improvement and red for decline, with value labels and a change pill at the right.
useFor: Change between two states per item: before vs after, last year vs this year, plan vs actual, men vs women, A vs B, scores pre- and post-launch. Pass data as [{label, before, after}], set the two series names, colours, prefix / suffix and which direction is good.

subtitle.default: Score out of 100, before and after the redesign
subtitle.doc: small line under the headline (empty = none)

beforeLabel.doc: legend name of the first dot

afterLabel.doc: legend name of the second dot

suffix.doc: text after every number, e.g. "%", " pts"

showValues.doc: print the before and after values beside the dots

showDelta.doc: show the change pill at the right

goodDirection.doc: "up" (increase is green) or "down" (decrease is green, e.g. cost, time)

zeroBased.doc: start the axis at zero (otherwise it zooms to the data range)

goodColor.doc: connector and pill colour for a good change

badColor.doc: connector and pill colour for a bad change

background.doc: page colour, or "transparent" to sit over other content

title: Dot tally (people as dots)
description: One dot per person in labelled groups; selected dots turn one by one from filled cream discs into open red rings while a huge counter runs; the total and a two-symbol legend land at the end.
useFor: Casualties, survey answers ("37 of 100 said…"), seats won, users affected, failure rates — a restrained alternative to a bar chart an agent can generate from two numbers.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/visual-investigation demo sPeople() (MIT, LemoLab) — idea, own SVG build

groups.doc: [{label, count, marked}] one grid per group; `marked` dots turn

ink.doc: colour of the filled dots and text

accent.doc: colour of marked dots and the big number

shuffle.doc: mark in seeded random order (false = row order)

total.doc: text for the final big figure (default: number of marked dots)

title: Funnel conversion
description: A conversion funnel: stage bars narrow in proportion to their value and grow in one after another from the top, labels with colour keys on the left, count-up values on the right, step-to-step "↓ 40%" conversion pills between stages and an overall conversion figure at the bottom.
useFor: Sales and signup funnels, hiring pipelines, checkout drop-off, content-to-lead stories, any "how many survive each step" breakdown. Replace stages, colours, prefix / suffix.

stages.doc: stages top to bottom [{label, value, color?}]; widths are proportional to value

subtitle.default: Users at each stage of the journey
subtitle.doc: small line under the headline (empty = none)

showConversion.doc: show the "↓ n%" pill between stages

showPercentInside.doc: print each stage share of the top inside its bar when wide enough

summaryLabel.doc: label of the final overall-conversion line (empty = hide it)

colors.doc: palette for stages without their own colour

title: Heatmap calendar
description: A GitHub-style contribution calendar: one rounded square per day, shaded in levels of the accent colour, popping in left to right with month and weekday labels, count-up stats and a less / more legend; the best day gets a pulsing ring. Reflows to a grid of mini-month calendars in square and vertical frames.
useFor: Activity over a year: commits, workouts, streaks, sales days, habits, support tickets, website traffic by day. Pass values (one number per day) and startDate, set the accent colour and unit; leave values empty to preview with seeded sample data.

values.doc: one number per day, up to 371 (empty = seeded sample year)

sampleSeed.doc: seed for the sample data used when values is empty

startDate.doc: date of the first value, "YYYY-MM-DD" (drives month labels and weekday alignment)

weekStart.doc: "sun" or "mon": which weekday is the top row

subtitle.default: Each square is one day, darker means more
subtitle.doc: small line under the headline (empty = none)

prefix.doc: text before total and best-day numbers

suffix.doc: text after total and best-day numbers, e.g. " commits"

lessLabel.doc: legend text at the light end

moreLabel.doc: legend text at the dark end

showWeekdays.doc: show Mon / Wed / Fri labels (strip layout)

emptyOpacity.doc: opacity of days with a zero value

background.doc: page colour, or "transparent" to sit over other content

title: Sankey flow
description: A Sankey diagram built from a list of weighted links: node bars grow column by column and curved ribbons, sized by value and coloured source-to-target, sweep across between them with labels and values; an optional highlighted node dims everything not connected to it.
useFor: Where things go: traffic to conversions, budget to departments, energy or cash flows, funnels with leaks, user journeys. Pass links as [{from, to, value}], set prefix / suffix and brand colours; works on a transparent background over footage.

links.doc: weighted links [{from, to, value, color?}]; nodes are created from the names, columns follow the flow direction

nodeColors.doc: optional node name -> colour overrides, e.g. {"Paid":"#E5487F"}

subtitle.default: Monthly sessions from first touch to paying customer
subtitle.doc: small line under the headline (empty = none)

suffix.doc: text after every number, e.g. "K", " users"

showValues.doc: print each node total (tall nodes: under the name, short nodes: next to it)

nodePad.doc: vertical gap between nodes of a column in u

align.doc: "justify" pushes end nodes to the last column, "left" keeps them where they land

highlight.doc: node name to spotlight at the end (empty = none); unrelated nodes and links dim

colors.doc: palette used for nodes without an override

background.doc: page colour, or "transparent" to sit over other content

title: Stacked area flow
description: A smooth stacked area chart (or centred streamgraph) revealed left to right by a wipe: layers swell over the timeline, a dashed scrubber follows the reveal edge with a running total, the legend values count with it, and the axis and gridlines sit quietly behind.
useFor: Composition over time: revenue by product line, traffic by source, energy mix, users by plan, time spent by activity. Replace xLabels and series; set baseline "center" for a streamgraph look.

xLabels.doc: labels along the x axis (years, months, ...)

series.doc: layers bottom to top [{name, values[] (one per x label), color?}]

baseline.doc: "zero" = stacked area from the axis, "center" = streamgraph centred on the middle

subtitle.doc: small line under the headline (empty = none)

showGrid.doc: horizontal gridlines with value labels (zero baseline only)

showLegend.doc: legend with live values, beside (16:9) or below (1:1, 9:16)

showScrubber.doc: dashed line and running total that follow the reveal edge

totalLabel.doc: word before the running total (empty = number only)

colors.doc: palette for series without their own colour

title: Timeline ruler with event cards
description: A ruler of years glides under a fixed playhead dot; every event pins a card (date, image or gradient, title, one line) with a spring pop while the camera pans between events and the big odometer year counter rolls through the years in between. Horizontal on 16:9/1:1, vertical on 9:16.
useFor: Company history, product roadmaps, "history of X" videos and about-us sections: pass `events` (date, title, body, optional image).

default.title: The first sketch
default.body: Two people, one whiteboard, a very large idea.

default.title: First product ships
default.body: The beta goes out to a hundred early users.

default.title: Rebuilt from scratch
default.body: A new platform for the next decade.

default.title: Today
default.body: Still sketching on the same whiteboard.

events.doc: [{date: "1998" (a 4-digit year is parsed), title, body?, image?: public path, icon?: name}]

scale.doc: 'linear' = gaps proportional to years (clamped) · 'even' = equal gaps

title: Number counter
description: Huge thin-mono counter that ticks or odometer-rolls through dwell keyframes, with unit, label and derived readouts (pressure, light, temperature, percent).
useFor: Depth/altitude/speed meters, growing stats, countdowns, progress percentages and scoreboards.
avoid: Set label, unit ('' to hide 'm'), readouts [] and keyframes — defaults are the DEPTH dive sample.

keyframes.doc: [[frame, value], …] monotone-cubic; put two close keys to dwell (slow down) near a landmark

mode.doc: roll (odometer digit strips with motion blur) | tick (re-typeset each frame) | lock (digits spin, lock one by one) | scramble (glyph noise + trail + drop) | flap (split-flap tiles) | clock (time-lapse clock)

label.doc: small tracked label above the number

decimals.doc: decimal places (tick mode; roll mode uses integers)

readouts.doc: derived stats under the number: pressure | light | temp | percent | rate

layout.doc: center (big, standalone) | hud (top-left overlay block like video23)

gauge.doc: semicircle gauge above the number (video17 anticipation meter); centre layout only

size.doc: number size in px at 1080p (auto-shrinks to fit)

labelSize.doc: label size in px at 1080p (centre layout)

linkBackdrop.doc: ocean backdrop darkens with the value (log scale) like a dive

lockStart.doc: lock / scramble / flap modes: frame the first character locks (or flips)

lockStep.doc: lock mode: frames between one character locking and the next (a sixteenth note at your tempo)

lockOrder.doc: lock / scramble: ltr | rtl character lock order

glyphs.doc: scramble: glyph set the unlocked digits flicker through (empty = digits)

accentOnLock.doc: locked characters flash in the accent colour for 6 frames

flashFrame.doc: one-frame brightness flash when a character locks

progressBar.doc: thin accent progress bar under the number while it locks

flapFrom.doc: flap mode: starting value (default = first keyframe value); ends on the max keyframe

flapStagger.doc: flap mode: frames between tiles starting to flip

flipFrames.doc: flap mode: frames one tile flip takes (0.26 s = 8)

callout.doc: flap mode: text that pops under the number after the last flip (e.g. "×2")

clockStart.doc: clock mode: start time in seconds since midnight (25200 = 07:00)

clockRate.doc: clock mode: [[frame, rate]] time-lapse speed; the clock integrates it

speedTag.doc: clock mode: show ×N TIME-LAPSE / ×1 REAL TIME tag

block.doc: block background colour behind the number (hook look, e.g. #FFD60A); "" = none

kicker.doc: hook line slamming in above the number

rollDuration.doc: block hook: seconds of the scale slam

title: Card stack cascade (bento + focus)
description: Feature cards scale in from 30 % with a fade, staggered 4 f apart, into a bento grid (or a row, or a fanned deck) with a gentle idle float; then one card flies to the centre and grows to ~60 % of the frame while the rest dim to 40 % and defocus, and everything settles back.
useFor: Feature overviews in launch videos, website sections, pricing / plan reveals: pass `cards` (title, body, icon, span "2x1"), choose `layout`, set `focusIndex`.

default.title: Realtime sync
default.body: Every change lands on every device in under a second.

default.title: Automations
default.body: Hand the boring parts to a workflow that never sleeps.

cards.doc: [{title, body?, icon?: bolt|shield|chart|chat|globe|spark|lock|cog|user|db|cloud|star, image?: public path, span?: "2x1" | number of columns}]

focusAt.doc: frame when the focused card flies to the centre

unfocusAt.doc: frame when everything settles back (0 = never)

dimTo.doc: opacity of the other cards during focus

title: Poll results bars
description: A poll card: the question types in, option bars fill one after another to their share with counting percentages, then the winner locks in with a glow and a tag while the rest dim; a vote total ticks up.
useFor: Poll and survey results, "you voted" reveals, audience-choice moments, A/B vote summaries, quiz answers and social engagement posts.

values.doc: one number per option — percentages or raw votes (normalised to a share of the sum)

totalVotes.doc: vote total shown at the bottom (counts up)

background.doc: frame colour, or "transparent" to overlay content

barColor.doc: colour of the non-winner bars, or "auto" (ink, softened)

cardColor.doc: card fill, or "auto" (a lighter tone of the background)

title: Split-screen compare
description: Presentation layout: headline, two perfectly synced panels (line-art vs colour by default) with colour-coded labels, stat lines and a footnote.
useFor: Before/after, A vs B, two tools / two styles / two renderers of the same thing.

headline.default: Same blueprint, two ways to draw it

subheadline.default: Same scene, same camera, same timing. Only the renderer changes.

footnote.default: ※ Export time = time to turn the finished 8-second animation into an MP4.
footnote.doc: small grey footnote at the bottom

left.doc: {label, color, desc, stat, src, style} for the left (top in portrait) panel; style lines|color|mono|sepia|warm

image.doc: public/ image shown in both panels when a side has no own src (empty = procedural plate)

layout.doc: 'panels' = two side-by-side (stacked in portrait) panels, 'wipe' = one frame with a moving divider, 'ledger' = full-bleed halves: divider drops, the bad half desaturates with a red tint, two counters race, a stamp lands on the divider

introWipe.doc: divider draws on and the panels open outward from it

push.doc: shared camera push amount over the whole motion (0.14 = +14 %)

fadeOut.doc: panels fade to black over the last 0.5 s (chrome stays)

build.doc: both panels are revealed in sync by a rising scan line after the intro

counters.doc: ledger: [{label, value, unit?, prefix?, bad?, decimals?}] for the two halves; bad = desaturated + red tint

stamp.doc: ledger: stamp text on the divider after both counters settle

dividerDrop.doc: ledger: frames the divider takes to drop in

badTint.doc: ledger: red tint multiplied over the bad half

title: Testimonial card carousel
description: Customer quote cards with a big quote mark, star rating, avatar, name and role rotate through a centre stage; neighbouring cards peek in scaled and dimmed, pager dots follow.
useFor: Social proof sections, customer-love videos, case-study teasers, landing-page testimonial strips, review roundups and app-store style praise.

default.quote: We cut our weekly reporting from a full day to twenty minutes. It simply works.
default.name: Maya Rivers

default.quote: Setup took one afternoon and the whole team was using it by Friday.
default.name: Dev Patel

default.quote: Support answered in minutes and actually fixed the problem. Rare these days.
default.name: Lena Ortiz

default.quote: The best purchase we made this year. Our customers noticed the difference.
default.name: Sam Okafor

testimonials.doc: array of {quote, name, role?, rating?(0-5)} — up to 10

holdFrames.doc: frames each card is held in the centre

moveFrames.doc: frames of the glide to the next card

heading.doc: small caption above the cards (empty to hide)

background.doc: frame colour, or "transparent" to overlay content

cardColor.doc: card fill, or "auto" (lighter than the background)
